text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. To get good results, users practise prompt engineering — writing clear instructions that help the model give useful answers. LLMs can write texts, translate languages and answer questions quickly. However, they have limits: they sometimes produce false information, and their knowledge depends on the data they were trained on. For this reason, it is always wise to check important facts yourself.
